sentences.text: This is the second application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No.494/2023 registered at Police Station Madhavnagar, District Ujjain (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 363, 366(A), 376(2)(N) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Section 5L/6 of the POCSO Act.
sentences._hearing_file: Yash vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: The applicant is in custody since 02/10/2023.
sentences._hearing_file: Yash vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: 2. As per prosecution story, on 23/09/2023 the brother of the prosecutrix lodged an FIR at Police Station Madhavnagar by stating that his minor sister prosecutrix went to the School for examination, but she did not come back.
sentences._hearing_file: Yash vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: They tried to search her everywhere but could not find her.
sentences._hearing_file: Yash vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: During the investigation, it is found that applicant abducted the minor prosecutrix and took her with him and committed rape upon her.
sentences._hearing_file: Yash vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: Accordingly, offence has been registered against the applicant.
sentences._hearing_file: Yash vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is an innocent person and he has been falsely implicated in this offence.
sentences._hearing_file: Yash vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: He is in custody since 02/10/2023.
sentences._hearing_file: Yash vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: His earlier bail application was dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to renew his prayer after examination of the prosecutrix.
sentences._hearing_file: Yash vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: Now prosecutrix has been examined before the trial Court and she has turned hostile and not supported the case of the prosecution.
sentences._hearing_file: Yash vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: Applicant is permanent resident of Ujjain district and is not having any criminal past.
sentences._hearing_file: Yash vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: Final conclusion of the trial is likely to take sufficient long time.
sentences._hearing_file: Yash vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 January, 2024.json

sentences.text:
Under the above circumstances, prayer for grant of bail may be considered on such terms and conditions, as this Court deems fit and proper.
4.
sentences._hearing_file: Yash vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / State opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection by submitting that prosecutrix was minor at the time of incident, therefore, applicant is not entitle for bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Yash vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 January, 2024.json

sentences.text:
5. Perused the impugned order of the trial Court as well as the case diary.
6.
sentences._hearing_file: Yash vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 January, 2024.json

sentences.text:
After considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, nature and gravity of offence,
arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant and also taking note of the fact that prosecutrix has been examined before the trial Court and she has turned hostile; she categorically stated in her statement that present applicant has not committed any rape upon her and she voluntarily went with the applicant and solemnized marriage with him and final conclusion of the trial will take sufficient long time.
sentences._hearing_file: Yash vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: In these circumstances, I deem it proper to release the applicant on bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Yash vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: Therefore, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.
sentences._hearing_file: Yash vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 January, 2024.json

sentences.text: 7. It is directed that applicant be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.75,000/- (Rupees Seventy Five Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance before the trial Court, as and when required.
sentences._hearing_file: Yash vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 January, 2024.json

sentences.text:
He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) Cr.P.C.
Certified copy as per rules.
